intro.text: Shai's Essence Marks are what she asks for in return for working for the arbiters.
A highly complex soulstamp that briefly Forges someone's memories, past and soul, among the most powerful stamps a Forger can make.

description.text: Realmatically, the Mark reshapes the person's spiritual aspect so it fits the history written for them.
The people of MaiPon use Essence Marks on themselves to gain skills, adopt disguises, change their personality or body, or rewrite their memories.
Several peoples, including the Grands, the Mulla'dil Strikers and the Dzhamarians, hold Essence Marks to be blasphemy.

items.text: Gaotona volunteered as a test subject, and Shai tried pieces of her work on him. The stamp explaining why Ashravan became emperor failed.
That stamp finally took once Shai grounded it in Ashravan's bond with Gaotona.
Shai reached the final stage, merging all her earlier stamps into one.
Shai finished the Essence Mark and stamped Ashravan with it, and it took.
A copy of the Mark, left with Gaotona as a book, showed Shai had added touches to steer Ashravan toward the ruler he had once meant to be.

A Mark is made of hundreds of stamps, each covering a small piece of the history or personality to change. Each is tested to make sure it takes, then all are linked in a lattice on another object and tied to one final keystone stamp, the only one that needs pressing. Making them requires deep knowledge of the person and of the new history.
Essence Marks are the hardest soulstamps to make, often taking years, and work only when tuned to one particular person.

Faint red smoke rises as the soul resists the stamp. A Mark holds for a day at most, so it must be reapplied every twenty-four hours; after years of steady use, the stamp may no longer be needed. A Mark can be built to let its wearer remember, grow and change, but memories from a Mark fade within an hour of stopping.
With practice and study, Marks can be made that last much longer than a day.
One Mark makes Shai a scholar who speaks a dozen languages, from Fen to Mulla'dil, and knows many cultures, the sciences, mathematics and the world's political factions.
Another gives her the skills of a woodsman and hunter for surviving in the wild.
A Mark that turns Shai into Shaizan, a warrior trained for fifteen years by the Teullu. It took her two years to make.
